# Tab group

Figma: standalone symbol `Tab group`, node `2317:69213` (page Components, `1:28`).
Not a variant set. Measured as an instance inside
[App header + top navigation](AppHeader.md) (`2317:69206`).

A wrapping row of [Tab single](Tab.md).

## Markup

```html
<div class="v27-tab-group" role="tablist" aria-label="Sections">
  <button type="button" role="tab" class="v27-tab" aria-selected="true" id="t1" aria-controls="p1">Tab 1</button>
  <button type="button" role="tab" class="v27-tab" aria-selected="false" id="t2" aria-controls="p2">Tab 2</button>
  <button type="button" role="tab" class="v27-tab" aria-selected="false" id="t3" aria-controls="p3">Tab 3</button>
</div>
```

Second-level tabs:

```html
<div class="v27-tab-group v27-tab-group--sub" role="tablist" aria-label="Subsections">
  ...
</div>
```

`role="tablist"` needs an `aria-label` when there is more than one on a page - "Sections"
and "Subsections" above - or a screen reader announces two identical tablists.

## Classes

| Class | What it is |
|---|---|
| `.v27-tab-group` | the wrapping row |
| `.v27-tab-group--sub` | second-level tabs, dropped to Sm |

## Values

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| gap | **0 down, `--v27-spacing-ml` (24px) across** |
| wrap | on |

The asymmetric gap is deliberate: wrapped rows sit flush so the tab underlines form a
continuous rule rather than leaving a stripe of background between them.

## The size modifier lives on the group

Level 2 tabs are 14px where level 1 is 16px. Figma applies that as an **instance override**
on the nested group, not as a variant of Tab single - so it is a modifier on the group, and
the tab itself has no size axis.

That is worth knowing before adding a size axis to Tab single: the design file does not
have one, and the difference is a property of the level, not of the tab.

## All classes in this component

`.v27-tab`, `.v27-tab-group`, `.v27-tab-group--sub`
